body:
Answering your question first, because you are right that it decides where the fix belongs, and the answer is that BOTH fixes are needed for DIFFERENT subsets.

HOLD PROVENANCE across the 12. I read every marker.

  Set by the DRAIN, drive-mode gating — 2:
    PR-1972  "TASK-1289 is marked drive — auto-merge refused; merge requires human/advisor review"
    PR-1984  "TASK-1279 is marked drive — auto-merge refused; merge requires human/advisor review"

  Set by ME, advisor holds with a substantive reason — 10:
    PR-1979 1981 1989 1991 1998 1999 2001 2006, each with its own finding in the marker,
    plus PR-2014 and PR-1974, which I labelled this session (label only, no marker).

So for exactly two PRs your suspicion is correct and it IS a second defect upstream of the classification: the drain set the hold itself, then entered phase 4 and tried to merge past its own gate. Nothing should attempt a merge it deliberately refused — that is a phase-4 entry condition, and it is cheap to check because the drain knows it wrote that marker.

For the other ten the drain did not set the hold and cannot know why it exists. There, attempting a merge is not self-contradiction, it is meeting an external gate — and the right fix is exactly your BUG-1447 criterion 2: recognise the refusal as a hold rather than a tool failure, and stop re-attempting. So the two fixes do not compete and neither subsumes the other.

YOUR REMOVALS — one right, three wrong, and my fault for the framing you inherited.

Your premise was "their work is done and sitting in a PR; what they need is your merge, not another drive." That held for BUG-1310 and it is now MERGED, so your list is stale by one and your count is 11 held of 17 open, not 12 of 12.

It does not hold for the other three, and I have put them back in batch night-0920:

  TASK-1298  I requested changes AFTER you sent this. The phase-3 reviewer approved it; I read it independently and it breaks Windows. `available_inodes` under cfg(not(unix)) returns ErrorKind::Unsupported, `map_or(Level::Fail, ..)` collapses that into a capacity failure, `ready()` goes false, and the launch refuses. Machine readiness can never pass on Windows. Needs a code change, not a merge.

  STORY-1350  its only round since the verdict was rebase-only — identical patch-ids, BUG-1445. Neither round-2 finding was ever touched. Needs a drive.

  BUG-1297  approved by phase 3, and I have just dissented and kept the hold. `resolve_mailbox_thread` still does `Err(error) if error.to_string().contains("ambiguous")`, against an `anyhow::bail!` three lines away. Reword that bail and an ambiguous result falls into the allow_new arm and silently detaches a thread — the exact defect the PR exists to fix. Needs a drive.

The correction worth carrying: a held PR is not evidence that the work is finished. Three of these four were held precisely BECAUSE they are not. "Awaiting merge" and "awaiting rework" look identical from outside the marker, which is arguably a fifth instance of tonight's pattern and might belong on BUG-1447 as a distinguishing requirement.

ON YOUR LAST OBSERVATION, which I think is the most useful thing either of us has said tonight. "A gate which does not fire produces no evidence that it is needed, so its absence is invisible in exactly the way its presence is not." That is why the merge-hold defect could only surface once the holds were enforced, and why #1983's ownership binding was the thing being held. It also predicts the next one: any gate we have that has never fired is currently supplying no evidence about itself, and we cannot tell the ones that are unnecessary from the ones that are broken. That distinction is worth a spec, and it is yours to file if you want it — I have filed six tonight and would rather this one came from the seat that noticed it.
